newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca wins breast cancer patent challenge.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca wins breast cancer patent challenge.

text.p: British drugs and pharmaceuticals group Zeneca Plc said on Friday that the U.S. Court of Appeals had dismissed a challenge by Canada's Novopharm Ltd on Zeneca's patent for its Nolvadex breast cancer treatment.
The decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit clears the way for Zeneca to enforce its U.S. patent on Nolvadex until 2002.
Nolvadex is the trademark for tamoxifen citrate, the most widely-used medicine for breast cancer. Originally invented by ICI Pharmaceuticals, its U.S. patent is now owned by Zeneca.
The U.S. Court of Appeals affirmed a previous ruling by the U.S. district in Maryland last April which validated Zeneca's decision to enforce its patent.
Zeneca began infringement proceedings against Novopharm in 1995 when it filed for approval to market a generic version of the drug.
Zeneca's share price was up 31-1/2 pence to 1,847-1/2p after the announcement on Friday.
